instruction: Use ANSYS Workbench to complete a Steady-State Thermal analysis. Before starting the work, launch ANSYS Workbench with `C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v261\Framework\bin\Win64\RunWB2.exe`. Physical problem: One-dimensional steady-state heat conduction through a rectangular steel block. Coordinate system and geometry: - Use the global Cartesian coordinate system. - The heat conduction direction is the global X direction. - The block length is along the X direction. - The block occupies: - 0 ≤ X ≤ 100 mm - 0 ≤ Y ≤ 10 mm - 0 ≤ Z ≤ 10 mm - The left end face is the face at X = 0 mm. - The right end face is the face at X = 100 mm. Model parameters: - Block size: 100 mm × 10 mm × 10 mm - Material: Structural Steel - Use steady thermal material properties for steel: - Thermal conductivity k = 50 W/(m·K) - Use a consistent unit system in Workbench. - Use a mesh that includes nodes or elements on the mid-length section at X = 50 mm. Boundary conditions: - Left end face at X = 0 mm: - Prescribed temperature = 100 °C - Right end face at X = 100 mm: - Prescribed temperature = 20 °C - All other external faces are adiabatic. Analysis type: - Steady-State Thermal analysis. Save requirements: - Use C:\Users\user\Desktop as the working location. - Save the Workbench project file as: C:\Users\user\Desktop\wb_conduction.wbpj - Save the MAPDL-equivalent database file as: C:\Users\user\Desktop\wb_conduction.db - Save the MAPDL-equivalent thermal result file as: C:\Users\user\Desktop\wb_conduction.rth Run the solver to completion and ensure a result file is generated.
